chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), that he said:
The stingy person is the one who is stingy with regards to what Allah has obliged upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a stingy person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) defines the stingy person (al-bakhil) not merely as one who hoards wealth, but specifically as one who withholds what Allah has made obligatory upon them, such as Zakat or Khums. This links the ethical vice of stinginess directly to the failure in religious duty, a concept emphasized in Shia jurisprudence where Khums is a primary pillar of wealth purification. By focusing on obligatory dues, the hadith elevates stinginess from a personal character flaw to a spiritual negligence that disrupts the covenant between the believer and God.

en.basel-kadem: 6.	With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Abu’l-Jahm, from Musa bin Bikr, from Ahmad bin Sulayman, from Abu’l-Hasan, Musa bin Ja’far, peace be upon them both, that he said:
The stingy is the one who is stingy with regards to what Allah has obliged upon him.
